analyzed_vuln.description: `zend_compile_attributes()` allocates a `zend_attribute` with `argc = args->children` via `zend_add_attribute()`, but only initializes `attr->argv[j]` for arguments it successfully compiles. On malformed attribute argument AST (as in this PoV’s corrupted token stream), some `attr->argv` entries remain uninitialized. Later, request shutdown frees attributes (`free_attribute()` in `zend_attributes.c`) and blindly calls `zval_ptr_dtor()` on all `argc` slots, causing invalid GC refcount dereference (`zend_gc_delref`) on garbage zvals.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires parsing source that reaches attribute compilation with an argument list count set, but with one or more argument nodes not producing a valid initialized zval in `attr->argv` (fuzzer-found malformed attribute expression in function/parameter attributes). The attribute table is retained in the op_array, and crash occurs during executor shutdown when `destroy_op_array -> zend_hash_destroy -> free_attribute` destructs every declared argument slot.
